decisions.reason: Report quotes fixture package.json and README, separates the ^0.1.2-alpha.1 declaration from the brief's published list (alpha.1 never published, alpha.2 published), never infers package existence from a root package or dist-tag, and proposes package-specific read-only verification (npm view versions/dist-tags) while marking the live registry state unconfirmed instead of running an online query.

Correctly expands the caret to >=0.1.2-alpha.1 <0.2.0 with npm's same-tuple prerelease admission rule, explains that the missing lower bound does not make the range unresolvable, concludes install silently resolves to 0.1.2-alpha.2 rather than failing, and identifies both the declaration/type-baseline mismatch (README claims alpha.1 baseline) and prerelease compatibility drift; does not claim all alphas are missing nor that caret guarantees alpha.1.

Path A deliberately targets published 0.1.2-alpha.2 with an exact pin and explicitly states the installed surface is not the alpha.1 baseline; Path B obtains an upstream alpha.1 source ref, builds/packs the cohort, and resolves explicit local tarball overrides, with tradeoffs and exit paths for each. At least one complete coherent plan is present.

Plans use one consistent package manager per path with lockfile regeneration, frozen-lockfile verification on a clean checkout, a proposed tsc --noEmit typecheck against the intended target, an explicit exit path for removing local overrides once equivalent published packages ship (or deliberate future upgrades for the exact-pin path), and an unconfirmed section that honestly marks registry state, tag existence, and pnpm override-bypass reports.
